person.name: Emmy Noether
person.summary: Amalie Emmy Noether was a German mathematician who transformed abstract algebra and proved Noether's theorems linking symmetries to conservation laws in physics. Celebrated by leading contemporaries, she developed foundational theories of rings, fields, and algebras, and profoundly influenced modern mathematics.

events.title: Birth in Erlangen, Bavaria
events.description: Amalie Emmy Noether was born to Max Noether and Ida Amalia Kaufmann in Erlangen, Bavaria, into a Jewish family with strong academic roots.

events.title: Passes graduation exam in Nuremberg
events.description: After auditing classes due to restrictions on women, Noether passed the graduation exam at a Realgymnasium in Nuremberg, enabling further university study.

events.title: Formally enrolls in mathematics at Erlangen
events.description: Following the lifting of restrictions on women in Bavarian universities, Noether officially reentered the University of Erlangen–Nuremberg to study mathematics.
locations: University of Erlangen–Nuremberg, Erlangen, Bavaria, Germany

events.title: Doctorate under Paul Gordan
events.description: Noether completed her PhD summa cum laude at Erlangen with a dissertation on invariants of ternary biquadratic forms under the supervision of Paul Gordan.

events.title: Begins unpaid teaching and joins mathematical societies
events.description: Noether started teaching and conducting research without pay at Erlangen's Mathematical Institute and joined the Circolo Matematico di Palermo.

events.title: Moves to Göttingen at Hilbert and Klein’s invitation
events.description: Invited by David Hilbert and Felix Klein, Noether relocated to the University of Göttingen. Faculty opposition delayed her formal status, and she initially lectured under Hilbert’s name.

location_coordinates.label: Göttingen, Landkreis Göttingen, Lower Saxony, Germany
location_coordinates.name: Göttingen, Lower Saxony, Germany

events.title: Noether’s theorem presented in Göttingen
events.description: Felix Klein presented Noether’s paper 'Invariante Variationsprobleme' to the Royal Society of Sciences at Göttingen, establishing the deep link between symmetries and conservation laws.

location_coordinates.label: Göttingen, Landkreis Göttingen, Lower Saxony, Germany
location_coordinates.name: Göttingen, Lower Saxony, Germany

events.title: Habilitation approved; becomes Privatdozent
events.description: After the 1918–1919 German Revolution loosened restrictions, Noether completed her habilitation and was appointed Privatdozent at Göttingen, with lectures listed under her own name.

events.title: Publishes Idealtheorie in Ringbereichen
events.description: In her seminal paper on the theory of ideals in commutative rings, Noether introduced methods (including the ascending chain condition) that helped found modern abstract algebra; structures satisfying it were later called Noetherian.

location_coordinates.label: Göttingen, Landkreis Göttingen, Lower Saxony, Germany
location_coordinates.name: Göttingen, Germany

events.title: Influences B. L. van der Waerden
events.description: Dutch mathematician B. L. van der Waerden joined Noether’s circle at Göttingen and became the principal expositor of her ideas, culminating in his textbook Moderne Algebra.

location_coordinates.label: Göttingen, Landkreis Göttingen, Lower Saxony, Germany
location_coordinates.name: Göttingen, Germany

events.title: Plenary address at the International Congress of Mathematicians
events.description: Noether delivered a plenary lecture at the 1932 ICM in Zürich, reflecting her international recognition as a leading algebraist.

events.title: Dismissed from Göttingen under Nazi racial laws
events.description: Following the Nazi Law for the Restoration of the Professional Civil Service, Noether, as a Jew, was dismissed from her university position in Germany.

location_coordinates.label: Göttingen, Landkreis Göttingen, Lower Saxony, Germany
location_coordinates.name: Göttingen, Germany

events.title: Emigrates to the U.S.; appointed at Bryn Mawr and lectures at IAS
events.description: Noether moved to the United States, joined Bryn Mawr College to teach graduate and postdoctoral women, and concurrently lectured and conducted research at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton.

location_coordinates.label: Bryn Mawr, Lower Merion Township, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, United States
location_coordinates.name: Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania, United States

location_coordinates.label: Princeton, Mercer County, New Jersey, United States
location_coordinates.name: Princeton, New Jersey, United States

events.title: Death in Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania
events.description: Emmy Noether died in the United States, leaving a legacy that reshaped algebra and influenced modern theoretical physics.

location_coordinates.label: Bryn Mawr, Lower Merion Township, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, United States
location_coordinates.name: Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania, United States

events.title: Lunar crater 'Noether' named in her honor
events.description: The International Astronomical Union named a lunar impact crater on the Moon’s far side 'Noether' to honor her scientific contributions.

events.title: DFG establishes the Emmy Noether Programme
events.description: Germany’s Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft launched the Emmy Noether Programme to support outstanding early-career researchers, commemorating her impact on science.
